messages.content: I booked the March 10-15 beachfront hotel, but the confirmation says two adults. Our 14-year-old was included when I searched, and the rate shown at checkout was for all three of us. The two-queen room and dates are right. Is this a problem?

The room itself permits up to four occupants, so three guests are allowed. The reservation record should still be corrected to show two adults and one child, especially for breakfast access, wristbands, and the hotel's occupancy records. Because she was included in the original search and the confirmed room supports three, ask the hotel to amend the guest count without canceling or rebooking.
Can I change it online, or should I call? I do not want the rate recalculated.

Do not use any online option that says it will reprice or replace the reservation. Call the hotel's in-house reservations desk, give them the confirmation number, and say the booking should list two adults and one 14-year-old at the existing confirmed total of $1,978.20. Ask them to make an occupancy-only correction and email a revised confirmation while you are on the call.
What exactly should I confirm before I let them touch it?

Have them confirm that the same two-queen room remains assigned for March 10-15, the mandatory total stays $1,978.20, and no extra-person, breakfast, or resort charge is added for your daughter. Also ask them to read back all three registered guests before sending the updated confirmation.
The cancellation section says a first-night deposit and mentions February 24 at 6:00 p.m. Central. I want to be clear on when I actually lose money.

The first-night deposit remains refundable if you cancel by February 24 at 6:00 p.m. Central. After that deadline, the cancellation penalty is one night's room charge plus the taxes and mandatory fees attached to that night; the reservation terms do not indicate that the full five-night stay becomes nonrefundable then.
So the guest correction does not reset that deadline?

It should not if the hotel processes it as a guest-count correction under the same confirmation number. Before approving the change, ask the agent to confirm that the original rate, deposit, and February 24 cancellation deadline remain unchanged. Then keep both the original and revised confirmations. If they say a new booking is required or quote a different total, stop and ask for a reservations supervisor rather than authorizing it.
